uncited: It builds on [Octree Path Computation](897-octree-path-computation.md) and operates alongside [Octree Neighbor Search](7782-octree-neighbor-search.md) and [Access Path Predictor](11650-access-path-predictor.md).
**Initialize and Validate:** Clamp AgentRadius.
Get nodes at Start and End positions by accessing the node Array.
Verify traversability using cached collision test results.
If Start or End nodes are not traversable (result $\neq +1$), return failure.
**Neighbor Collection:** Iterate from 0 to 7 to collect neighbor indices based on target axis (0 or 1).
Traverse the tree using DFS to collect all leaf nodes.
**Pathfinding (Lazy Theta*):** Initialize Cost, Parent, Open, and Closed arrays.
While Open is not empty, pop node $u$ with lowest $f(u)$.
If $u$ is End, reconstruct path and return.
For each neighbor $v$, calculate tentative $g(v)$.
Perform LOS check between parent of $u$ (or $u$ if $u$ is Start) and $v$.
If LOS is clear, set parent of $v$ to parent of $u$ (or $u$) and update $g(v)$ using direct distance.
Else, set parent of $v$ to $u$ and update $g(v)$ using distance from $u$ to $v$.
**LOS Method:** Perform a simple collision test between two points.
- **Agent Radius vs Node Size:** Simple comparison of octree node size with AgentRadius is insufficient.
- **Collision Test Cache:** Running a collision test every time is expensive.
- **Time Complexity:** Depends on SVO depth and branching factor.
At MaxDepth 6, BuildSVO takes 700 microseconds, FindPath takes 300 microseconds.
This method was developed for Unreal Engine 5 (UE5) as a simple SVO pathfinder for 3D pathfinding.
It was presented in a tutorial video by an unofficial source.
